subject: AI & Agents
title: Racial Bias in Facial Recognition
description: A micro-lesson that makes Racial Bias in Facial Recognition usable.

hook.text: A study found facial recognition misidentified Black women 35% of the time. For white men? Under 1%.

buildup.text: Training datasets overrepresented lighter-skinned faces, skewing the model's accuracy.

discovery.text: Joy Buolamwini's Gender Shades study exposed this gap and sparked global awareness.

twist.text: Police departments deployed these systems anyway. Innocent people were arrested.

climax.text: Several cities have banned facial recognition by police. Others expanded its use.

punchline.text: If the training data doesn't see you, the AI doesn't see you.

quiz.question: What caused facial recognition to perform worse on darker skin?
options: The cameras couldn't detect darker skin
Darker skin has fewer distinguishing features

details.summary: Facial recognition systems consistently perform worse on darker-skinned and female faces. Studies show error rates up to 34% for dark-skinned women versus less than 1% for light-skinned men.
details.whyItMatters: Biased facial recognition leads to wrongful arrests and surveillance of minority communities. Accurate, equitable identification technology is a civil rights imperative.
takeaways: Facial recognition error rates vary dramatically by race and gender
Dark-skinned women face the highest misidentification rates
Several cities have banned government use of facial recognition

faq.question: Why is facial recognition less accurate for people of color?
faq.answer: Training datasets have historically over-represented lighter-skinned faces. The AI learns to distinguish features it sees most often, resulting in poorer performance on underrepresented groups.

faq.question: Have wrongful arrests resulted from facial recognition errors?
faq.answer: Yes. Multiple documented cases show Black men being arrested based on incorrect facial recognition matches. These cases have fueled calls for bans and stricter regulation of the technology.
